On this battlefield, there was one chariot no arrow could stop, because God Himself was driving it. And I was the boy who fed its horses. Stay till the end, because you decide what I do next.

My name is Ishan. I was twelve. On the first morning of the great war at Kurukshetra, I held the reins of four white horses behind Arjuna's chariot. Two armies. Millions of soldiers. Conches so loud the ground shook.
Arjuna said, Krishna, take me to the middle. I want to see who I'm fighting. So Krishna drove us right between the armies. Grandfather Bhishma. Teacher Drona. Cousins. Uncles. Friends.

But then, something happened that no one expected. Arjuna's hands began to shake. His great bow slipped from his fingers and hit the ground. The greatest archer in the world sat down and cried. I can't fight my own family.
Wait, the war was about to begin, and our hero had given up? Then Krishna turned around, and looked straight at me.
So what should I do? Comment A, run to Arjuna and pick up his bow. Or comment B, stay still, and listen to what Krishna says. Part two, tomorrow.
